description:
List annotations: id, target, type, status, author and the quoted text, every one unless --by, --target, --type or --status narrows it; `--json` carries each one whole.

An agent re-reading its own annotations is the common case — a re-check resolves what is met and edits what still stands, and needs the ids to do it — so `--by` its own name lists them. The JSON form carries `message` too, so a re-check can tell what it already said without reading the log itself; `loom changes --by` lists the edits it suggested.

json.description: Print the annotations as JSON.

type.description: Only annotations of this type, by id or name.

name: loom_ai_annotations

description:
List each agent document: the working document it was drafted from and what has moved there since.

Before a large instruction, an agent checks its document here: a stale one is refreshed first, or the agent says what it is working against.

closed.description: List retained closed agent documents instead of active ones.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

name: loom_ai_drafts

description:
Print mode NAME in full: when it fits, what it is for, and what its report shows.

The quilt's own copy in .loom/agents/instructions/modes/ is printed, so an edit the author made there holds; with no .loom/agents/instructions/, the shipped one. `loom ai orient` lists every mode with its one line.

session.description: Log this call to the session.

name: loom_ai_mode

description:
Print the orientation documents followed by the quilt's live state, and with --session the end of that session's chat.

This is also how an agent joins a session it did not open: `loom ai orient --session <id>` prints the orientation, the quilt's live state, and the last messages of that session's chat with its command log, which is what a later sitting resumes from.

session.description: Attach to this session: also print the end of its chat and its command log. An id, a title, or a unique id suffix.

name: loom_ai_orient

description: Update an agent document from the working document it was drafted from, keeping its outstanding proposals.

dry_run.description: Say what would be refreshed and write nothing.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

name: loom_ai_refresh

description:
Write an annotation on TARGET: a key, an equation's qualified key, a master path, a work, or a project PDF; a MESSAGE of `-` is read from stdin.

An annotation carries its author, its time and the version of the text it was written on, and belongs to no session. A work is named by its reference, or by the key its entry has; one on a work with no --page is on the whole work. One on a page of a PDF -- a work's, or a project PDF by its path -- names the page with --page and the place with --quote (words on it), --box (a rectangle) or --stroke (ink), drawn with a --mark tool where it is not on words; `loom status --reading` lists those on cited works.

box.description: Anchor to a rectangle on the page, in points with the origin at the top left; ';' separates several. With --edit, where a drawn one stands now.

delete.description: Delete an annotation, with its replies; an agent deletes only its own. It is removed from the log, not marked.

dry_run.description: Say what would be written, and write nothing.

edit.description: Restate an annotation: a new body, --type, a look, or where a drawn one stands; never its anchor.

in.description: A claim about the node as read in this document: marked there, listed on the node's own page, absent elsewhere.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

mark.description: Draw it on the PDF page with this tool: a pin or words on the page in the --box, a box or an oval round it, ink or an arrow along each --stroke.

page.description: Page N of a PDF: a work's (TARGET its reference, or the key its entry has) or a project PDF by its path; with --quote, --box or --stroke.

quote.description: Anchor to this exact text: once in a key's own text, or on the page of a cited work given by --page.

reply.description: Answer annotation ID; the message is the reply.

resolve.description: Mark annotation ID resolved, with the message as why.

stroke.description: A line of ink or an arrow on the page, in points from its top left; repeat for more lines. With --edit, its lines now.

style.description: How it is drawn on words, over its type's.

type.description: The annotation's type, by id or name, from the quilt's annotation types; default none. With --edit, '' takes it off.

undo.description: With --resolve, open the annotation again: an undo is another event, never a removal.

weight.description: An underline's or a strike's thickness, in whole pixels.

name: loom_annotate

description:
Ask the person a question in TEXT, or with --paper for a paper you could not fetch.

A question waits in Review with its choices and a field for the person's own words; once they answer, `loom tasks` shows the answer until your next `loom since`, which reports it. A paper waits in Review with its link, for the person to fetch and add; the request closes once the work holds the document.

choice.description: One choice the person may pick; up to six. They may always answer in their own words.

for.description: A draft it is asked for, so the person can see it with that draft's; default the documents that read the place.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

link.description: With --paper: the http or https page you could not fetch it from, which the person opens.

on.description: What it is about: a result's label or id, a key, a work's id with :PAGE, or a document's path.

paper.description: Ask for a paper you could not fetch, by its reference's id; give --link.

want.description: With --paper: which document of the work.

name: loom_ask

description:
Scan, derive, render, and publish .loom/cache/site/, what the viewer is served. Exit 1 if any error-severity diagnostic exists outside the works nothing cites (the build is still published).

A whole build then removes what loom keeps for no purpose any more: from .loom/cache/ what this build does not name and nothing has written in the last hour, an agent's scratch fourteen days after its session last wrote, and a saved preview fourteen days after it was written; a build of --keys removes nothing.

A document is read from the HTML its compile made, and shows as its source until one has. Text no compile makes, a node no document reaches, a landmark, a comparison, is made by TeX as snippets. Rendering is cached per block by its inputs, which include loom's own version and, in a checkout, loom's code; --force renders everything regardless, and makes again every text TeX refused before. Only errors are listed; `loom lint` lists every diagnostic.

force.description: Render every block again, ignoring the cache and making again every text TeX refused.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

keys.description: Limit rendering to these keys and their masters; the manifest is always complete.

no_compile.description: Run no TeX: text no compile makes comes from the cache, else shows as its source.

name: loom_build

description:
List what waits on you, by document: each open suggested edit and each in-place edit since your last look to an open file agents may edit, cut by words; with ID, print the change's patch, which `git apply` takes as it stands.

The open files are the ones the viewer shows that are text, at most 1 MB, LaTeX's auxiliary files left out; your look holds the text of each one agents may edit as you last saw it, and `loom serve` takes your first when it starts. A place agents are denied is yours, and an edit there is never listed, whoever made it. Keeping and discarding are yours, never an agent's: keeping an in-place edit puts it into your look, keeping a suggested edit writes it into its file; discarding an in-place edit puts its old words back, discarding a suggested edit leaves the text as it is. A version of each document a write changes is kept first. Keeping says nothing about whether the mathematics is right, which is `loom accept`'s.

by.description: NAME's suggested edits, in every state.

document.description: Only the changes in the files DOC is made of.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

name: loom_changes

description:
Lint, then compile every document, then the closures asked for. Exit 1 on any failure; the CI command.

`loom lint` is the same check without LaTeX.

closures.description: Which statements' closures to compile after the documents: all of them, or none; stale compiles none yet.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

name: loom_check

description:
Run latexmk from a master's own directory into its compile folder, .loom/cache/tex/<stem>-<hash>/ (default: the default master), or for a key.

Compiling a key builds the document of its closure and runs latexmk on that, so `--with` previews a proposed diff and `--draft` a node that has no id yet: neither writes into the quilt. `--html` also makes a document's HTML as TeX makes it, which its fragments are cut from: the page, the fragment loom rebuilt from it, and how many of the document's nodes and blocks it places.

draft.description: Compile a node file not yet in the quilt.

html.description: Also make a document's HTML with TeX4ht, into .loom/cache/tex/<stem>-<hash>/html/, and say how much of it loom can place.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

session.description: Log this call to the session.

with.description: Substitute a unified diff, a .tex file, or a suggested edit's text (by its id) for KEY's text; the quilt is not touched.

name: loom_compile

description: Show what KEY depends on directly, through its statement and through its proof.

closure.description: The transitive statement closure in dependency order.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

session.description: Log this call to the session.

name: loom_deps

description:
Check the TeX toolchain and what loom needs of it, poppler, git, the author name and the viewer bundle; inside a quilt, also its engine, its generated files, its .gitignore and its config.

Each item is ok, warn (works, but you will hit it) or fail (a command you need will refuse), with the command that fixes it. Exits 0 when nothing fails and 2 when anything does; under --strict a warning counts as a failure. Without --repair it writes nothing; a tool is run only to ask its version or test what loom needs of it, and one that has not answered in 10 s is reported as hung.

json.description: Machine-readable report on stdout.

repair.description: Repair TeX first: install loom's own TeX, or put back what it lacks. Touches nothing outside loom's directory.

settle.description: Settle a write loom could neither finish nor undo as it stands, by the id the writes item gives: your files stay as they are, each suggested edit it wrote is recorded as the files show, and it is no longer said. The author's; refused in an agent's shell.

strict.description: Count a warning as a failure: exit 2 when any item warns.

name: loom_doctor

description:
Show everything downstream of ID: dependents, reference and inclusion sites, ledger rows, annotations. Reports; changes nothing.

With --proofs, only the proofs that cite ID themselves: where a hypothesis or a lemma is consumed, rather than everything that rests on it.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

proofs.description: Only the proofs that cite ID directly, each with the statement it proves.

session.description: Log this call to the session.

name: loom_downstream

description:
Draft an agent document NAME from a live working document: flat, in `.loom/agents/copies/`, with every label it defines derived.

A copy step records what each of its nodes began from, and who drafted it: `--as`, else the configured author; an agent that has not named itself is refused. A document of an agent's own needs no command: it is a file the agent writes where the quilt lets it. Starting a document from an old version of one is `loom history restore`.

dry_run.description: Say what would be written, and write nothing.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

section.description: Copy only this section or subsection and its descendants.

name: loom_draft

description: What is known of a result: its status, and every record about it. NAME is a draft's label or a node's id.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

name: loom_evidence

description:
Say whether formalization is on for this quilt on this machine, and whether loom can check its Lean here.

The person turns it on (`loom formal on`), which installs Lean, its toolchain and Mathlib and makes the quilt's Lean project; from then an agent writes Lean in the project, marks each declaration that states a result with `@[loom "LABEL"]`, and asks loom to check it (`loom formal check`). What Lean said is loom's own record, never an agent's.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

name: loom_formal

description:
Have loom check the quilt's Lean itself: rebuild the project from clean, read which declaration states which result (`@[loom "LABEL"]`) and the axioms each rests on, and replay the build in Lean's kernel, every step fenced, with no network and writes only in the project. Each result a declaration states gets loom's own record of what Lean said, which stops standing once its Lean or its statement changes.

Refused when formalization is off here, and from a shell that is itself fenced, such as an agent's sandbox, where the fence cannot be put up: ask through loom's tools instead.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

name: loom_formal_check

description:
Say where the person is looking in the viewer: the document, result, paper or session in front of them, the block at the top of the pane, the words they selected or the region of a page, and the annotation whose popup is open. A region or an annotation on a PDF page comes with a crop of the page around it, under .loom/cache/crops/.

The viewer tab they touched last reports it to `loom serve`, which keeps it in memory only. With nothing serving the quilt, or no tab open, it says so. Each thing is named with the link `loom link` prints.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object, the place as the viewer sent it beside it.

name: loom_here

description:
List the steps and stamps of this quilt, one per line; `loom history KEY` lists that key's versions and whether the head equals one.

A landmark, which `show` prints and `restore` starts a document from, is named by its name, its step, or `DOC@STEP`.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

key.description: A key, to list its recorded versions and whether its text now is one; with none, the history's steps.

name: loom_history

description:
Print a landmark's text.

The text of the landmark NAME as its step kept it, raw; with --plain, the paper without loom.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

plain.description: The paper without loom, its package line swapped for the macro block.

name: loom_history_show

description:
Check the history against its ledger.

Every step directory is walked against the ledger: missing or edited version files, preambles, copies, and ancestry that no longer resolves.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

name: loom_history_verify

description:
Print a patch inserting \label{<id>} on every untagged theorem-like environment and section in FILE, or write the patched copy with --to; with --next, print the next free id.

FILE is never modified.

fix_anchoring.description: Include line-anchoring repairs in the patch or written copy.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object; for a FILE, the patch is in it.

next.description: Print the next free id and nothing else; inserts nothing.

sections.description: Also label sections through subsubsection (default on).

session.description: Log this call to the session.

to.description: Write the patched copy here instead of printing a diff: outside the quilt's sources and .loom/, but for an agent's scratch, .loom/agents/scratch/SESSION/.

name: loom_id

description: Propose a correction of a node's text: written at once where no person has compared it, else filed for the person to take or decline, the compared text standing meanwhile.

body.description: The node's corrected text, as LaTeX; its header is kept.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

mention.description: A node the text mentions without resting on it.

why.description: What was wrong, for the person who compared it.

name: loom_library_correct

description: Have loom write a work's results from its TeX source, numbered by its stored PDF: loom's own extraction, never a compile. A work whose numbers only a compile could confirm waits for the person's act in the viewer.

item.description: A result of its source's survey, for --scope chosen.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

scope.description: What the drafts cite of it, every result, or the items --item names.

name: loom_library_digest

description: Give a stub its text, transcribed from its work's PDF or read from its TeX source: its words are checked to stand there, and how it was made is recorded as yours.

body.description: The result's text, as LaTeX, pointing at other nodes by their ids.

from.description: Read from the work's PDF, or from its TeX source.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

mention.description: A node the text mentions without resting on it; every other it names is a use.

pages.description: The page or pages it stands on, as the PDF numbers them (`12`, `12-13`), at most three; needed from a PDF and refused from the source.

name: loom_library_fill

description: A statement or a proof of the library with its neighbours: its header, its text, what it uses and mentions, its proofs, and what rests on it. NODE is its id.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

name: loom_library_node

description: Propose a node at a place of a work no node holds: a new statement of REF, its words checked to stand there; it reads as not checked until the person compares it.

body.description: The result's text, as LaTeX, pointing at other nodes by their ids.

from.description: Read from the work's PDF, or from its TeX source.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

mention.description: A node the text mentions without resting on it.

number.description: Its number as the work prints it.

pages.description: The page or pages it stands on, as the PDF numbers them, at most three; needed from a PDF and refused from the source.

taxon.description: What it is: lemma, theorem, definition, ...

title.description: The name the work gives it.

name: loom_library_propose

description: The library's results a draft rests on, through its citations and what those use in turn: WHAT is a draft's result (its id or label) or a document's path. Each says how it stands; a stub is one nobody has read.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

name: loom_library_rests-on

description: Search the library's statements, stubs among them, by their words, name, title and work.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

taxon.description: Only statements of this taxon (lemma, theorem, ...).

work.description: Only this work's statements: its id or its entry's key.

name: loom_library_search

description: The library's stubs: results known to stand in a work whose text nobody has read yet, which `loom library fill` gives their text.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

name: loom_library_stubs

description: What a node's text uses and mentions, and which nodes use and mention it. NODE is its id.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

name: loom_library_uses

description: A work: what loom holds of it and its outline, every result of its source digested or not. REF is its id.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

name: loom_library_work

description:
Print a markdown link to THING that the viewer can follow.

THING is a node or any key in it, a document's path, an annotation id, a session id, a work (its reference, or the key its entry has), or a file the viewer shows by its path (`notes/day1.md`, `--at` a heading's id; a PDF `--at page=N`; a text file `--at L12`). `--quote` carries words in a document, a project PDF or a work, which the viewer opens at and lights. The link's text is empty: the viewer names the thing itself, as `Theorem 3.1`, and keeps the name right when the document is renumbered; write your own words between the brackets to show those instead. A thing the viewer does not show is refused, with why.

at.description: A place in THING: a key inside the document or node, a heading's id in a Markdown file or notebook, page=N in a PDF, L and a line number in a text file.

page.description: A page of a work's PDF, from 1.

quote.description: Words to open at and light: on the work's page, on the PDF's page given by --at page=N, or at the place in a document; anywhere in it with no page or place.

name: loom_link

description:
Scan and print every diagnostic, each with its class.

A class says what kind of problem it is: latex, a problem in a document's LaTeX, a last compile that failed among them, and all the viewer shows a person; model, loom's model of the quilt (ids, \uses, links, copies, records), an agent's to keep; internal, loom's own difficulty or the integrity of its records. An error is a fault in what TeX compiles, or in loom's records; exit 1 on one. Fast: no LaTeX runs, and a compile's problem is read from the log the document's last compile left.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

nodes.description: One block per node id: what is wrong with its identity, and the superseded files.

session.description: Log this call to the session.

name: loom_lint

description:
Allocate an id and write nodes/<id>.tex, beside the default document, with a skeleton for TAXON; with --print, print the skeleton instead.

The node's `% !LOOM author:` line is whoever writes it: `--as`, else the configured author; an agent that has not named itself is refused.

dry_run.description: Say which id and file would be written, and write nothing.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

prefix.description: Allocate under this prefix instead of [quilt] prefix.

print.description: Print the skeleton without allocating an id or writing a file.

session.description: Log this call to the session.

to.description: The node file to write, instead of nodes/<id>.tex beside the default document.

name: loom_new

description:
Find ids by id, alias, title, taxon or tag; exact matches first.

A number as a reader sees it -- `Theorem 3.4`, `3.4`, `(3)` -- finds what each drafting document numbers so, the default document's first and marked; `--in DOC` asks one document only.

in.description: Resolve a number like `Theorem 3.4` in this document only.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

session.description: Log this call to the session.

name: loom_search

description: List this quilt's sessions, newest last, with the active one marked.

json.description: Print as JSON.

name: loom_session_list

description: Open a session and make it the active one.

dry_run.description: Say what would change and write nothing.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

name.description: What to call it; default untitled.

no_use.description: Create it without making it the active session.

name: loom_session_new

description: Change a session's title. Nothing moves: the id is the address and does not change.

dry_run.description: Say what would change and write nothing.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

name: loom_session_rename

description:
Say TEXT in a session's transcript, with what you marked since your last message; `-` reads TEXT from stdin.

The transcript is what the author reads afterwards. A person's message carries the annotations they wrote since the session's round opened that no message of it has carried yet, and with no TEXT it carries them alone. A `quilt:` or `cited:` link that names nothing the viewer shows is refused; `loom link` prints a correct one.

dry_run.description: Say what would change and write nothing.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

name: loom_session_say

description:
Report what people did since you last looked, and move your marker past it.

People's annotations and replies, whole, with the words they are on; what they resolved, deleted or reopened, and what they kept or discarded of your suggested edits; what they accepted, and every accepted key gone stale, with why; their edits to the research state, as a diff; what they said in a session's transcript; their answers to the questions you asked with `loom ask`; the boxes they set in the viewer, each as it last stood; and each other file the viewer shows that was added, changed or removed, by its path: not a .tex file, what a compile writes beside one, or the research state. Loom cannot tell who changed a file, so your own edits are listed too. Your first look reports what happened since the active session was last opened, and no files, having seen none. The marker is yours alone, one per name and one per session you look as, and kept on this machine only; a session's first look starts where your name's marker stands, and each look moves both. Over MCP the server looks as your conversation's session.

dry_run.description: Report, and leave your marker where it was.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

session.description: Look as this session, one conversation's: its own marker, whose first look starts where your name's stands. An id, a title, or a unique id suffix.

name: loom_since

description:
Print TARGET's LaTeX source: a key's own text, or a document flattened with every inclusion expanded in place.

This is how a reader or an agent gets the text of a result or of a whole paper. It writes nothing: there is no file to clean up, none to keep out of version control, and none to go stale against the author's next edit. A section's key prints the section with everything in it.

With --closure, a key is preceded by exactly the statements it depends on, in dependency order. A document is already whole, so --closure does not apply to one. With --at REF, the key's text as it stood then: the text an annotation was written against, the text last accepted, or a step of the history; --diff shows what has changed since.

at.description: The key's text at REF instead: an annotation's id, `accepted` (or `accepted:NAME`), or a step of the history.

closure.description: Everything TARGET depends on, in dependency order, then TARGET itself.

diff.description: With --at: a unified diff from that text to the key's text now.

session.description: Log this call to the session.

name: loom_source

description:
List every key with its computed state, cause if stale, and review facts; it exits 0 whatever it finds, and 2 only on an argument it refuses.

Annotations on works are not on keys and appear in no row; `--reading` lists them by work, and `--json` always carries them under `reading`. While `loom serve` runs, a document it last compiled with errors or into no PDF is listed too, and `--json` carries how each of its compiles stands under `compiles`.

detached.description: Keys whose annotations no longer find their quoted text.

explain.description: Why KEY is in its state, with the diff of what moved.

in_order.description: With --master: the document's keys in the order it prints them, sections and an agent document's own among them, each with its state.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

reading.description: List the annotations on works, by work; they are in no row and count toward nothing otherwise.

retired.description: Keys accepted once and defined by no document now.

session.description: Log this call to the session.

stale.description: Accepted keys whose text, closure or preamble moved since.

status.description: Keys carrying an annotation in this state.

type.description: Keys carrying an annotation of this type, by id or name.

name: loom_status

description:
File a suggested edit on KEY: --with NEW in place of --quote OLD, or beside it with --before or --after; without --quote, of the key's body.

The person keeps or discards it with `loom changes`: keeping writes it into the file, discarding leaves the text as it is, and `loom changes ID` prints the patch that takes it. An edit that names the annotation it --answers resolves that annotation when it is kept. `--before` with no quote puts the text at the head of the body, which is how a `\uses{…}` is proposed. `--withdraw EDIT` takes back one of your own while it is open; `loom changes --by NAME` lists the edits NAME suggested, in every state.

after.description: Put the new text right after the quoted words, or at the end of the body.

answers.description: The annotation it answers; keeping the edit resolves it.

before.description: Put the new text right before the quoted words, or at the head of the body.

comment.description: What to say beside it, in Markdown.

dry_run.description: Say what would be filed, and write nothing.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

quote.description: The words it replaces, once in the key's own text and inside the block, short of its \begin and \end; without it, the key's body.

with.description: The new text; '' deletes the quoted words, and - reads it from stdin.

withdraw.description: Withdraw suggested edit EDIT, one of yours still open, instead.

name: loom_suggest

description:
List what waits for an agent: what a person asked of agents, the questions and papers agents asked of the person, and each answer the person gave that the agent that asked has not seen since its last `loom since`.

Nothing is assigned or ranked: take what you can do (`loom tasks take ID`), and say what you produced (`loom tasks done ID --made ID`). An ask closes by what it produces, a stub read or Lean run on its result, whoever produced it.

all.description: Include asks that are closed or withdrawn.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

name: loom_tasks

description: Answer TASK, a question the person asked of an agent, in TEXT.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

name: loom_tasks_answer

description: Say what you produced for TASK. The task closes when what it asked for exists, which loom checks, not when you say so.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

made.description: What you produced: a node's id, a suggested edit's id. Repeat for each.

name: loom_tasks_done

description: Say that your session is working on TASK, so the person sees it taken; refused while a live session of another works on it. Over MCP your session is your conversation's; in a shell, the active one.

json.description: Print the report as one JSON object.

name: loom_tasks_take

description:
Write a page: TARGET `state`, the quilt's research state; `-` reads TEXT from stdin.

A page is a reading the person edits directly and an agent writes here, never by hand; it says who wrote it, and it is never a source. Once the page exists, --base must be the hash it had when you read it, which `loom ai orient` prints, so an edit you have not seen is never overwritten: a stale base is refused, with that edit shown. A link that names nothing the viewer shows is refused, as in a message. Every write is recorded in the history, with who made it.

base.description: The page's hash as you read it; required once the page exists.
